title: Hebron (entry), in The New Encyclopedia of Archaeological Excavations in the Holy Land, vol. 2
author: Avi Ofer
publisher: Israel Exploration Society / Carta (ed. Ephraim Stern)

summary: Ofer's NEAEHL synthesis of his own 1984-1986 Judean Hills Survey Expedition excavations at Tell Rumeida (Tel Aviv University, with the Staff Officer for Archaeology of the Civil Administration and the Israel Exploration Society), the main modern excavation campaign at the site before Eisenberg's later salvage digs. Ofer reports that the Middle Bronze Age 'cyclopean' city wall (built of massive, roughly hewn boulders) continued in use, and reads the 11th-10th century BCE (Iron I / early Iron IIA) as the settlement's demographic and political peak within the Iron Age sequence, on the strength of the surveyed regional settlement pattern rather than a fully excavated Iron IIA town plan at Tell Rumeida itself. This project cites Ofer for exactly that claim and its evidentiary basis (a peak-period inference from Judean-hills regional survey data, not an excavated Iron IIA fortification/building plan at the site) — see eisenberg-ben-shlomo-2017-tel-hevron for the later excavation seasons that narrow what is actually dated to that specific window, and ussishkin-2021-cyclopean-wall-hebron for a published challenge to the cyclopean wall's construction date itself.
